title: Designing Identity and Access Management
objective: Distinguish authentication from authorization, and manage principals, conditions, and resources according to the principle of least privilege.

sections.title: Authenticate people, applications, and external systems distinctly
paragraphs: For human access, choose federation and MFA; for workloads, choose roles and temporary credentials; and for external systems, choose integrations with trust conditions. A design that shares long-term access keys and prevents you from distinguishing principals makes revocation, auditing, and limiting the scope of a breach more difficult.

When investigating an authentication issue, check the IdP, MFA, tokens, role trust policies, time, and related CloudTrail events. Successfully authenticating a user and authorizing that user to access the target resource are separate decisions.

sections.title: Evaluating Effective Permissions Across Multiple Boundaries
paragraphs: For authorization, effective permissions are evaluated by combining identity-based policies, resource-based policies, session policies, permissions boundaries, organization policies, and explicit denies. Explicitly identify the principal, action, resource, and conditions that require permission, and do not assume administrator permissions by default.

To assume an IAM role managed by another AWS account, the caller must have permission for `sts:AssumeRole`, and the conditions in the trust policy of the target role must also be satisfied. When creating the target role in the customer account, its permissions policy should allow only the required prefix and operations for the target bucket. When delegating access to a third party, an external ID can also be configured as a trust condition. A bucket policy is an additional boundary to apply when an explicit denial or further conditions are required; it is not always mandatory when the role and bucket are in the same customer account. The solid lines in the figure represent the role-assumption request, the response containing temporary credentials, and the request to S3 using those credentials. The dashed lines represent the trust conditions checked by AWS STS.

sources.label: Access to AWS Accounts Owned by Third Parties

sections.title: Continuously Review Permissions
paragraphs: Access design does not end with the initial grant. Regularly review unused permissions, employee departures or transfers, role changes, emergency access, and exceptions, and retain the owner, purpose, expiration date, and approval records.

Break-glass access is not intended for routine use in place of normal least privilege. Define the activation conditions, MFA, short validity period, monitoring, and post-use review, and always verify why it was used and what impact it had.

sources.label: SCS-C03 Exam Guide: Identity and Access Management

checkpoints.prompt: You are designing administrative access integrated with an HR system. If you want to promptly revoke access for departing employees and require MFA, which policy is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use an IdP and federation, and apply MFA and role-based temporary sessions.
choices.explanation: This integrates HR information with authentication and revocation while avoiding long-term credentials.

choices.text: Distribute an administrative access key shared by everyone in the department.
choices.explanation: You cannot identify the individual or revoke access.

choices.text: Disable MFA and make the password permanent.

checkpoints.prompt: An audit firm's tool assumes an audit IAM role in the customer's AWS account A. The customer moves the audit logs to an S3 bucket in a different AWS account, B. B owns the objects, and they use SSE-S3. Which settings allow the tool to keep using the same role to retrieve objects only under the approved prefix?

choices.text: Allow the role in A to call s3:GetObject on objects under the approved prefix in both the role's permissions policy in A and the bucket policy in B.
choices.explanation: AWS evaluates the role's permissions policy in the requesting account A and the bucket policy in the resource-owning account B. A cross-account retrieval needs permission on both sides.

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObject under the approved prefix in B only in the role's permissions policy in A.
choices.explanation: An administrator in A cannot grant access to a bucket owned by B on their own. The bucket policy in B must also allow access.

choices.text: Add account B to the role's trust policy in A. Leave the bucket policy in B as it is.
choices.explanation: The trust policy determines who can assume the role in A. It does not give a tool that already assumes that role permission to read objects in B.

checkpoints.prompt: You are designing a break-glass procedure that permits production administrative operations only during emergencies. Which control is most appropriate?

choices.text: Have everyone routinely use emergency administrator credentials.
choices.explanation: This eliminates least privilege and auditability.

choices.text: Do not retain records of emergency operations.
choices.explanation: This prevents the impact from being assessed afterward.

choices.text: Define the activation conditions, MFA, a short validity period, operation monitoring, and a post-use review.
choices.explanation: This enables emergency access to be tracked and controlled as an exception.
